briefings.title: Find your purpose after major setbacks: Katie Piper on how to adapt, reinvent and lead
briefings.tldr: Advocate and author Katie Piper reflects on surviving a 2008 acid attack at age 24, reframing profound trauma into self-authored identity and founding a leading burn-rehabilitation charity.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Advocate and author Katie Piper reflects on surviving a 2008 acid attack at age 24, reframing profound trauma into self-authored identity and founding a leading burn-rehabilitation charity. She explains why resilience and discomfort are prerequisites for personal growth, and why vulnerability and empathy are critical leadership traits.

## Identity and Overcoming Adversity
* **Self-Authored Identity:** Society conditions women and girls to anchor their value in fleeting assets like youth and beauty.
  * *Perspective:* Trauma and age reveal that identity is self-authored, freeing individuals from rigid societal expectations at different life stages.
* **Reframing Tragic Setbacks:** Life is unpredictable, but individuals control their reaction rather than the initial event.
  * *Key Quote:* "You could say, 'Oh my gosh, my life was over at 24 and interrupted and destroyed.' Or you could say, 'Oh my gosh, I got an unexpected chance to restart my life at 24.' [...] I didn't lose my power, I stepped into my power." — Katie Piper

## The Modern World, Resilience, and Discomfort
* **The Perils of Seamless Pathways:** Modern conveniences (dating apps, career-pivoting, online shopping, fast fashion) teach people that everything should be easy and seamless.
  * *Negative Coping:* When challenges arise, people frequently quit or turn to negative coping mechanisms (drugs, alcohol, gambling, excessive shopping) rather than building resilience.
* **Resilience as True Confidence:** Confidence is not smooth skin, a luxury watch, or a specific physical figure.
  * *Definition:* True confidence is the deep-seated resilience to know that you are malleable, can evolve, and will bounce back from whatever life brings.
* **Embracing Discomfort:** A little bit of suffering is character-forming; growth happens when individuals lean heavily into discomfort rather than shying away from dark times.

## Burn Survivors, Stigma, and the Katie Piper Foundation
* **Founding the Charity:** Founded by Katie Piper in the UK in 2010 as a burn rehabilitation charity to bridge the massive gap between acute life-saving care (skin grafts, plastic surgery) and long-term functional rehabilitation.
  * *Evolution:* Initially started as a grant-giving trust to send UK burn survivors to France for specialized multi-disciplinary care (physios, occupational therapists, speech therapists).
  * *Current Scale:* More than a decade later, the Foundation operates the UK's first and only residential burn rehabilitation facility in the northeast of England near St. Helens and Liverpool.
* **Acid Attacks Data and Legal Context:** Acid attacks are on the rise across the UK and Europe.
  * *Drivers:* Acid remains a weapon of choice for perpetrators because it carries lighter sentencing (categorized simply as Grievous Bodily Harm / GBH in UK courts) compared to knife or gun crimes, lacking severe legal deterrents.
  * *Demographics:* Data shows acid attacks are not exclusively male-on-female violence; female perpetrators exist, and victims include both men and women across gang-based and honor-based violence.
* **Challenging Visible Difference:** Society fears what it does not know or see (including visible differences, ethnicity, and stigmatized diseases).
  * *Milestone:* The 2012 London Paralympics significantly advanced public perception of individuals with disabilities, mirroring broader improvements in diversity across media, beauty, and professional environments.

## Leadership, Empathy, and the World Economic Forum
* **Role as Cultural Leader:** Attending the World Economic Forum Annual Meeting 2026 in Davos as a cultural leader to champion empathy and human connection.
* **Vulnerability in Leadership:** Showing vulnerability and discussing mental health are not weaknesses; they function as a superpower that demonstrates how a leader handles pressure and adversity.
* **Core Leadership Tenet:** Social change, empathy, and emotional intelligence are just as critical in leadership as finance and policy.

> "Nobody ever found their why on a mediocre day. So actually you're going through something right now that you can't see an end to or you're feeling 'why me'. Why don't you ask yourself instead of 'why me', 'what now?'"
> — Katie Piper

> "Identity is very much self-authored, and you don't have to conform to society's idea of identity at certain stages of your life."
> — Katie Piper

> "Confidence is not smooth skin or the latest watch or a certain figure. It's the confidence to know that whatever happens to me in life, I will bounce back. I will reinvent."
> — Katie Piper

briefings.title: GTC SJ 2026: Physical AI for Healthcare Robotics - Simulation-First Design & Accelerated Development
briefings.tldr: Driven by a looming global healthcare crisis—including a doubling of surgical caseloads over the next decade and 40% of US orthopedic surgeons currently over age 60—engineering teams are deploying the NVIDIA Physical AI ecosystem (featuring foundation models, physics-based simulations, and digital twins) to transition healthcare robotics from slow, model-based programming to accelerated, simulation-first design and scalable autonomy.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Driven by a looming global healthcare crisis—including a doubling of surgical caseloads over the next decade and 40% of US orthopedic surgeons currently over age 60—engineering teams are deploying the NVIDIA Physical AI ecosystem (featuring foundation models, physics-based simulations, and digital twins) to transition healthcare robotics from slow, model-based programming to accelerated, simulation-first design and scalable autonomy.

---

## The Healthcare Robotics Crisis & Simulation-First Data Pipelines
- **Demographic Pressures:** Global healthcare faces a massive supply-and-demand crisis, compounded by aging populations and a shrinking pool of practicing surgeons across both soft and hard tissue specialties.
- **The Data Bottleneck:** Developing physical AI for healthcare requires a complex, traditionally manual four-stage pipeline: data curation/annotation, synthetic data generation, model training, and deployment.
- **The Three-Pillar Technology Shift:**
  - **Generative Physics & Foundation Models:** Leveraging models like NVIDIA Cosmos to generate physically accurate data without exhaustively solving complex partial differential equations by hand.
  - **Explainable Reasoning:** Adopting vision-language-action (VLA) foundation models (such as Groot and Alpamo) that not only execute commands but explain their reasoning—vital for clinical explainability and safety.
  - **Accelerated High-Fidelity Simulation:** Shifting away from slow, pixel-by-pixel rendering toward real-time simulated environments using Gaussian models and sensor-to-action deployment pipelines.

## Surgical Robotics: Soft Tissue & Autonomous Interventions
- **Data Collection and Teleoperation Limitations:** Surgical robots collect immense amounts of data, but manual annotation is hindered by legal hurdles and a lack of standard surgical ontologies.
  - **Ontology Standardization:** Led by Dr. Filippo Filiberti and partners at SAGES, researchers are defining surgical gestures and anatomical landmarks (e.g., critical vessel annotations, hernia repair landmarks) to power video-language action models.
  - **Limitations of Model-Based Approaches:** Custom model-based approaches for surgical suturing hit a performance ceiling of approximately ~60% stitch-to-stitch success rates and do not scale across procedures.
- **Hierarchical Policies & Imitation Learning:**
  - **Johns Hopkins & Smart Surgical Research:** Dr. Axel Krieger discussed utilizing imitation learning and transformer models on the Da Vinci Research Kit and suturebot systems.
  - **Cholecystectomy Automation:** Using hierarchical policies (high-level language policy determining surgical phase feeding into low-level kinematic execution policies), researchers achieved fully autonomous gallbladder removal (clipping and cutting the bile duct and cystic artery) across 16 hours of ex-vivo porcine data without human intervention.
- **Open H Initiative & Groot Fine-Tuning:**
  - **Massive Dataset Release:** The community published **Open H**, the largest surgical robotic dataset to date, containing over 150,000 trajectories with kinematics (1 terabyte), which achieved 1,000 downloads within days of its Monday release.
  - **Model Performance:** Fine-tuning the **Groot** model (specifically *Groot-age*) on the Open H dataset and suturebot data out-performed state-of-the-art suturing models while requiring only 33% of the training data.

## Collaborative Laparoscopic Platforms & Edge Compute Integration
- **Maestro System Architecture (Moon Surgical):** 
  - **Form Factor:** A two-armed, cart-based collaborative laparoscopic system deployed in the US and EU with broad indications for holding and positioning instruments. 
  - **Edge Compute Powerhouse:** Bedside IGX platform equipped with an A6000 GPU and Azure capture card, processing laparoscopic video feeds, dual 3D depth cameras (RGB-D on the lighthouse and lower system), and high-resolution force sensors on the robotic arms.
- **Advanced Features & Closed-Loop Feedback:**
  - **Scope Pilot:** Enables surgeons to control three instruments with two hands by having the camera automatically follow manual instrument movements.
  - **Optimized Arm Deployment:** Because arm configurations vary wildly across thousands of procedures and operating room layouts, Moon Surgical is using **Isaac SIM** (running the full software stack) and **Cosmos Transfer** to generate synthetic camera imagery and close the data gap for setup optimization.

## Hard Tissue Robotics: Humanoid Architecture for Orthopedics
- **Hard Tissue vs. Soft Tissue Challenges:** 
  - Soft tissue systems rely on remote, teleoperated multi-arm consoles. Hard tissue (spine, long bones, joints) traditionally utilizes single, rigid robotic arms tethered to stationary infrared navigation cameras—analogous to trying to hammer a nail with one hand.
- **LAM Surgical Innovations:**
  - **Upper-Torso Humanoid Architecture:** CEO Yossi presented a first-of-its-kind system featuring two operating arms synchronized with a dynamic third arm housing vision sensors.
  - **Instrument Agnosticism:** Unlike locked ecosystems requiring proprietary vendor tools, the system allows surgeons to rapidly calibrate and operate third-party instruments and implants.
  - **Collaborative OR Environment:** Designed to collaborate safely in close quarters with both sterile and non-sterile personnel while handling hundreds of diverse, non-proprietary surgical instruments.

---

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Autonomous Laparoscopic Functions Timeline:** Procedure-level autonomy will take time to reach productization, but lower-risk collaborative functions in laparoscopic surgery—such as camera control (already deployed by Moon Surgical), suction holding, tissue traction, and port placement—will arrive over the next few years — **Dr. Axel Krieger**
- **Foundation Model Evolution:** Rapid iteration continues on foundational architectures, noting that newly trained VLA iterations like *Groot v1.6* quickly become foundational baseline points for ongoing clinical data fine-tuning — **Sean Hoover / Moon Surgical Team**

---

## Notable Quotes
> *"Simulation is hopefully underutilized in surgical training. The people that are actually operating on people they sit down at a console with me and they do actually learn how to operate on real humans. And this is not fair. It's not ethical. And that's why we're trying to really work hard to make this better."*  
> — **Dr. Filippo Filiberti**

> *"We don't have to get to the point where we've done 50,000 surgeries to simulate 50,000 surgeries and thankfully we now have the tools to do this."*  
> — **Moon Surgical Presenter**

> *"You give your kids a fork and knife and you put it in the hand in your in their hands. You say eat nicely... but now it's not pasta, now it's rice... This training is a challenge and it's an iterative process that needs to be done."*  
> — **Yossi**

briefings.title: Kavak's Playbook for Rebuilding a Company Around AI
briefings.tldr: Kavak transformed its used-car marketplace into an AI-native company where agents handle 96% of customer interactions and 95% of transactions, outperforming human sales teams by over 2x.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Kavak transformed its used-car marketplace into an AI-native company where agents handle 96% of customer interactions and 95% of transactions, outperforming human sales teams by over 2x.

## Company Overview & Business Model
* **Core Operations:** **Kavak** operates as a vertically integrated used-car marketplace in Latin America, handling car purchases, refurbishment, sales, financing, personal loans, and logistics.
* **Shift from Transactional to Relational:** **Alejandro Maza Ayala** explained that Kavak shifted from measuring basic transactional metrics (cars bought/sold) to managing 10 million customers in its database where long-running agents maximize customer lifetime value (LTV).
* **Scale of Agent Deployment:** Between 100,000 and 200,000 agents are instantiated daily, each equipped with its own virtual machine, multi-year memory, and hard goals.

## Engineering the Agentic Architecture
* **Agentic Harness Over Workflows:** **Alejandro Maza Ayala** noted that after previously using multi-agent graphs and workflows (which worked well until December), Kavak transitioned to a robust harness where each customer gets an individual virtual machine, CLI access to every company API/tool, and a long-term goal of maximizing LTV.
* **Evals as the Primary Engine:** **Alejandro Maza Ayala** emphasized that Kavak spends as much engineering time, tokens, and money on building evaluations (evals) as it does on building the agents themselves, measuring first and foremost true business conversion and customer happiness rather than superficial KPIs.
* **Token ROI Tiers:** **Alejandro Maza Ayala** outlined Kavak's token expenditure framework:
  * *Tier 3 (Most Valuable):* Direct ROI tracking through agents performing core organizational jobs.
  * *Tier 2:* Indirect evaluation via developer output in codebases.
  * *Tier 1:* Unmeasured usage of generic plugins or chat tools (where ROI is unknown).

## Performance and Real-World Applications
* **Superhuman Sales Agents:** **Alejandro Maza Ayala** stated that Kavak built complex sales agents—not just customer support bots—that handle 20,000 SKUs, financing, insurance, and trade-in quotes. These agents tripled NPS, initially converted 50% better than human teams, and now convert over **2.1x** better.
* **Financial Underwriting at Scale:** **Alejandro Maza Ayala** noted that car loans are typically approved in under 3 minutes in Mexico due to deep customer and vehicle data integration.
* **The "AI CEO" Experiment:** To test organizational limits, Kavak deployed an AI agent as the CEO of a single city in Mexico (**Cuernavaca**). Over its first 6 weeks, the AI CEO aimed to double profits, ultimately achieving a **1.5x (50% increase)** in monthly profit by micromanaging forecasts, customer data, and issuing daily voice-note plans to 800 physical workers.
* **Human-Agent Collaboration in Mechanics:** **Gabriel Vasquez** and **Alejandro Maza Ayala** discussed "El Mike," a physical-world sidekick inspired by *Ratatouille* that guides Kavak's ~800 mechanics in Mexico through inspections and repairs, reducing warranties by **26%**.

## Organizational Transformation & Training
* **Top-Down Restructuring:** **Alejandro Maza Ayala** stressed that successful AI adoption requires a top-down redesign of APIs, systems, and company structure rather than simply handing ChatGPT to existing teams.
* **The Jedi Academy:** Kavak launched an internal training program called the Jedi Academy, ranging from the CEO and AI engineers to mechanics, where participants spend 6 weeks learning to build and launch state-of-the-art AI agents to production.
* **Human-in-the-Loop Feedback:** Rather than discarding failed agent interactions to a dead-end support queue, Kavak routes human-assisted exceptions back into building new skills and training data for the broader agent fleet.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Alejandro Maza Ayala** predicts that by **2035**, with the current rate of capability improvement, AI agents will be fully capable of performing complex leadership roles such as a company CEO.
* **Alejandro Maza Ayala** claims that companies looking for incremental AI adoption (achieving only 6% to 10% efficiency gains by keeping old factory-style structures) will be disrupted by new AI-native companies undergoing Schumpeterian creative destruction, drawing a parallel to how factories failed to gain 3x productivity until they fully redesigned around electricity and small dynamos rather than coal shafts and belts.

## Notable Quotes
> "I'm investing more today in tokens than in knowledge workers. We could build superhuman agents. This means that by every dimension that matters, our agents would outperform the best human if we had ever hired."
> — **Alejandro Maza Ayala**

> "If my customer is happy, they'll buy a car, they'll get their loan approved... they'll sell a car to us and that's the like first check. Like did it convert? And that's where most things break. Like I see companies measuring number of calls or minutes during the call... but that doesn't really work."
> — **Alejandro Maza Ayala**

> "Economic value in humanity for the past 4,000 years has been delivered by organizations, not by individuals. So what you want to self-improve and to engage in that loop is the organization that can deliver more economic value."
> — **Alejandro Maza Ayala**

briefings.title: Peter Steinberger: What Happens When 4.7 Million People Let It Cook
briefings.tldr: Peter Steinberger shares how his side project OpenClaw exploded from a simple WhatsApp relay built out of personal annoyance into an open-source juggernaut with 4.7 million weekly downloads, and explains why developer velocity depends entirely on building things that genuinely excite you.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Peter Steinberger shares how his side project OpenClaw exploded from a simple WhatsApp relay built out of personal annoyance into an open-source juggernaut with 4.7 million weekly downloads, and explains why developer velocity depends entirely on building things that genuinely excite you.

## Origins and Product-Market Fit
- **The Annoyance Catalyst:** 
  - Created in November 2025 because there was no easy way to send prompts from a phone to a computer to check on coding agents while away.
  - Built a WhatsApp relay in about an hour by letting the model cook in a terminal session.
- **The Evolution to OpenClaw:** 
  - Expanded to Discord after receiving a community pull request, temporarily naming the project Claudius, then Claudebot, before settling on OpenClaw.
  - Initially struggled to get Twitter followers to care about the agent's magical, proactive feel until testing it in WhatsApp group chats and witnessing strong emotional reactions (amazement and fear).
- **Viral Explosion:** 
  - Launched a Discord server during the first week of January 2026 for people to watch him build in the open.
  - A launch daemon ensured the agent kept running after pressing Ctrl+C, resulting in 800 messages upon waking up and immediate viral pickup by tech reporters.

## Scale, Burnout, and the Open Source Toll
- **Staggering Metrics:** 
  - Reached over 18,000 different people opening an issue or pull request, totaling over 111,000 contributions, with almost 3,000 people contributing commits.
  - Downloads bottomed out at 835,000 weekly downloads in May before peaking at an all-time high of 4.7 million weekly downloads.
- **The Cost of Attention:** 
  - The sudden influx of reporters, leaked phone numbers, and security reports nearly caused Steinberger to delete the entire project and severely strained his mental health.
  - Shifted time away from building toward legal work (setting up a 501(c)(3) American nonprofit) and defensive security hardening.
- **Security and Maintenance Pitfalls:** 
  - Fought off a wave of security reports, noting that only about 0.3% of scanned skills were actually malicious (out of 67,000 scanned).
  - Accumulated around 9,500 configuration options, making the codebase increasingly difficult to maintain and breaking user setups when shipping updates.
  - Faced sudden dependency disruptions when Anthropic gave roughly 24 hours' notice before disabling subscriptions for Opus, which OpenClaw had been heavily optimized around.

## Philosophy of Building
- **Personal Brand Over Products:** 
  - Emphasizes that any product can be forked or cloned, making a personal brand vital before starting a new venture.
  - Believes programming is just a means to an end; the real passion lies in building.
- **The Power of Fun:** 
  - Discovered that "fun is velocity"—weeks spent enjoying the build process resulted in a visibly better product, whereas maintenance work slowed momentum to a halt.
  - Advises building software that solves personal annoyances, noting that user #1 should be yourself and users #2 through #20 should be friends.
- **Current Team and Infrastructure:** 
  - The OpenClaw foundation now has 10 people on payroll and is actively hiring additional roles, including a CEO.
  - Nvidia stepped in early to provide personnel who took over much of the project's security workload.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Open Source Agent Capabilities:** Peter Steinberger claims that perpetually running, proactive AI agents are entirely possible today, but are currently bottlenecked by token costs and the lack of efficient systems to handle large context resets without burning excessive money on idle computations.

## Notable Quotes
> "My source of inspiration is usually being annoyed... It's hard to compete with someone who's just there having fun. Fun is velocity."  
> — Peter Steinberger

> "Everything that you can build can be forked or cloned, but your name cannot. So your personal brand is way more important than any single product that you ever will start working on."  
> — Peter Steinberger

> "Your dependencies business model is your business model."  
> — Peter Steinberger

briefings.title: Private Credit's Clock is Ticking w/ Glenn Schorr & Ken Worthington | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 72
briefings.tldr: Steve Eisman, joined by Glenn Schorr of Evercore and Ken Worthington of JP Morgan, explores the looming refinancing crunch in private credit software loans, the mechanics of retail broker cash yield optimization via agentic AI, crypto use cases versus Bitcoin’s store-of-value thesis, and a booming second-quarter earnings season for major investment banks.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Steve Eisman, joined by Glenn Schorr of Evercore and Ken Worthington of JP Morgan, explores the looming refinancing crunch in private credit software loans, the mechanics of retail broker cash yield optimization via agentic AI, crypto use cases versus Bitcoin’s store-of-value thesis, and a booming second-quarter earnings season for major investment banks.

## Retail Brokers, Cash Yields, & Agentic AI
* **Brokerage Cash Revenue Model:** 
  * Retail brokers (such as Charles Schwab and LPL) generate a substantial portion of their profits from "lazy cash" — uninvested customer sweep balances from which the firm captures interest spread or fees.
  * **Ken Worthington:** Notes that if an investor manages their cash actively (e.g., in money market funds), the broker's fee is significantly lower than the spread earned on lazy cash.
* **Agentic AI Threat & Friction:**
  * **AI Efficiency vs. Profitability:** Agentic AI could theoretically automate cash optimization by paying bills and sweeping idle funds into higher-yielding products based on spending habits, potentially squeezing broker cash net interest income.
  * **Regulatory & Systemic Hurdles:** Worthington notes that systemic safeguards and regulators are unlikely to allow frictionless, micro-optimized checking-account swapping across financial institutions without triggering stability risks.
  * **Execution Reliability:** Worthington points out that AI agents are currently incorrect the majority of the time when managing money and must reach near-perfect reliability before high-net-worth investors will relinquish control.
* **Resilient Financial Models:**
  * **Glenn Schorr:** Prefers large diversified banks (e.g., JP Morgan) and wealth managers (e.g., Morgan Stanley) that bundle primary checking accounts with comprehensive services like trust, estate, and tax planning, making customer switching friction high.
  * **Charles Schwab Valuation Debate:** Eisman questions whether Schwab's business model long-term equilibrium should rely on customer inaction, while Worthington maintains a **Buy** recommendation on Schwab, arguing that clients retain the option to manually optimize and firms can package their own agentic services.

## Private Equity & Private Credit
* **Private Credit Inflows & Redemptions:**
  * **Glenn Schorr:** Inflows into wealth-channel direct lending products have nearly dried up, while redemption requests remain elevated, with most funds exceeding the 5% per quarter limit.
  * Schorr notes that while underlying software investments continue to generate cash flow and margins, fundraising momentum has stalled.
* **Private Equity Monetizations & Valuations:**
  * PE performance has underperformed public markets for the first time since 2008–2009, struggling to keep pace with the Magnificent Seven.
  * While some managers (e.g., **KKR**) reported record monetizations, others face sluggish exit markets despite record highs in public equity indexes, creating pressure from LPs demanding liquidity.
  * **Vintage Multiples Challenge:** Assets purchased during the 2020–2021 zero-interest-rate environment at high multiples are facing extended holding periods as companies grow into their valuations.
* **The Software Refinancing Time Bomb:**
  * **Steve Eisman:** Highlights the public "SaaS apocalypse" (e.g., ServiceNow down over 50% from its peak) and asserts that private equity software company valuations must similarly be down roughly 50%.
  * **Refinancing Timeline:** Eisman predicts a major reckoning starting in late 2027 and accelerating in **2028 and 2029**, when approximately **$270 billion** of software maturities held by financial sponsors come due for refinancing.
  * **Lender vs. Sponsor Standoff:** Schorr notes that restructuring conversations involve a spectrum of outcomes, from a few keys handed back to lenders, to stalemate negotiations, to opportunistic credit funds stepping in with higher yields and stricter terms to take over positions.

## Crypto, Stablecoins, & Bitcoin's Relevance
* **Crypto Ecosystem & Token Proliferation:**
  * **Ken Worthington:** Views crypto not strictly as a fiat currency hedge, but as an asset class where blockchain technology and token utility co-exist and proliferate (citing blockchains launched by Coinbase and Circle).
  * **Bitcoin vs. Alt-Chains:** Worthington distinguishes Bitcoin as a single-use store of value facing concentration risk, whereas blockchains like Ethereum and Solana support active application development and token trading.
* **Stablecoins & Payment System Friction:**
  * **Steve Eisman:** Argues that payment incumbents like Visa and Mastercard are elite, deeply entrenched operators unlikely to cede territory to new entrants, making Circle's push into the core payment system extremely difficult.
  * Worthington points to cross-border remittances, 24/7 trading settlement layers, and foreign-market dollarization as viable near-term use cases for stablecoins like USDC alongside ongoing traditional experimentation.

## Big Bank Earnings Review
* **Second-Quarter Results Overview:**
  * **Glenn Schorr:** Characterizes big bank earnings as stunning, noting that fundamental drivers are operating at near-peak efficiency.
  * **Investment Banking & Trading Performance:** Investment banking revenue surged **38%**, and trading revenue jumped **47%** (with equity trading revenues up approximately **68%** and margin balances on borrow up **50%**).
  * **Asset Management & Expenses:** Asset and wealth management posted **7%** organic growth amid all-time high markets, while operating leverage remained positive with expenses well-controlled.
  * **Deposit Competition:** Deposit costs are ticking up due to real competition, representing the only mixed fundamental area in an otherwise exceptionally strong quarter.

## Notable Quotes
> *"The business model is dependent upon basically the customer being lazy. And it just bothers me. I'm just going to throw it out there. I just think that that's not an equilibrium long-term."*
> — **Steve Eisman**

> *"My opinion on private credit is we are a year away from finding out what we're going to really need to find out because you've got companies whose valuation given what's happened in the public SaaS apocalypse... are down something like 50% from where it was bought."*
> — **Steve Eisman**

> *"My belief is over time that the technology is good, the blockchains will proliferate, the tokens will proliferate along with the blockchains, and a market will form."*
> — **Ken Worthington**

briefings.title: Using AI to Increase Your Intelligence & Enrich Humanity | Dr. Fei-Fei Li

people.name: Fei-Fei Li
people.role: Professor of Computer Science, Stanford University

briefings.tldr: AI systems are powered by the convergence of massive internet-scale data, advanced neural network algorithms, and high-performance GPU computing.
briefings.summary_markdown:
### TL;DR
AI systems are powered by the convergence of massive internet-scale data, advanced neural network algorithms, and high-performance GPU computing. While AI excels at pattern recognition, statistical generation, and processing explicit data, it fundamentally differs from human cognition, which is driven by biological agency, motivation, and inaccessible personal experiences.

---

### ## Foundations and Evolution of Artificial Intelligence
* **Biological Origin of Vision:** **Dr. Fei-Fei Li** notes that 540 million years ago, the evolution of photoreceptive cells in simple ocean trilobites sparked the Cambrian explosion of animal speciation. In human brains, approximately **50% of cortical activity** is dedicated to visual function, making vision a cornerstone of both biological and artificial intelligence.
* **Neural Network Parallels:** **Dr. Fei-Fei Li** explains that modern neural network algorithms trace their inspiration back to the **early 1950s**, aligning with neuroscientists Hubel and Wiesel recording hierarchical visual cells in mammalian brains. Today's neural networks run on **hundreds of billions to trillions of parameters**.
* **The Big Data Turning Point:** **Dr. Fei-Fei Li** launched the **ImageNet project** in **2006** at Princeton, collecting **15 million internet-scale images** across **1,000 object categories** because existing algorithms lacked sufficient training data. This data scarcity was solved by converging ImageNet, mature neural networks, and **GPU computing** around **2012**, dropping classification error rates from random chance (1 in 1,000) down into the teens.

### ## Transition from Vision to Language and Video
* **Natural Language Processing:** **Dr. Fei-Fei Li** highlights that the **Transformer paper** published in **2016–2017** shifted the AI frontier from vision to natural language. Utilizing vast text data on the internet, companies like OpenAI and Google built models that led to the **ChatGPT moment in 2022** (taking roughly 5 years).
* **Video Generation and Dynamics:** **Dr. Fei-Fei Li** states that in **January 2024**, Sora was released, opening the floodgate for video generation. By training on massive internet video datasets, models learned plausible physical movements (such as a cat running toward a mouse) through statistical pattern matching rather than explicit muscle-structure programming.
* **Limitations of AI vs. Human Learning:** **Dr. Fei-Fei Li** contrasts AI with children: a young child learns what a "kitty cat" is after seeing only **3 to 10 cats**, whereas AI requires downloading billions of internet images. Furthermore, deeply personalized thoughts, abstract art, and individual emotional histories are never uploaded to the internet and remain completely inaccessible to AI.

### ## AI in Healthcare and Scientific Discovery
* **Biomedical Research:** **Dr. Fei-Fei Li** and **Andrew Huberman** discuss how AI can revolutionize scientific discovery by synthesizing vast amounts of cross-disciplinary data (e.g., combining neuroscience and olfactory research) at speeds unattainable by the human brain.
* **Robotic Surgery:** **Dr. Fei-Fei Li** shares a personal example of her father's complex liver surgery performed using the **da Vinci robot system** driven by a human surgeon, resulting in **10 times less blood loss** than typical traditional surgeries. 
* **Data Scarcity in Medicine:** **Dr. Fei-Fei Li** cautions that highly complex, vascular organs like the liver lack abundant surgical training data across global patient pools, meaning fully autonomous surgical robots require careful human-machine collaboration until simulation environments improve.

### ## Human Agency, Emotion, and Societal Impact
* **Preserving Human Agency:** **Dr. Fei-Fei Li** emphasizes that agency, motivation, and dignity are essential to humanity. AI should be deployed as a tool to augment and empower human communication and learning rather than strip away human autonomy.
* **Lack of True Emotion:** **Dr. Fei-Fei Li** clarifies that chatbots do not feel empathy or pain; when a model says "I'm sorry you're sick," it is executing pattern recognition based on training text, lacking the genuine biological memory of suffering that a human friend possesses.
* **The Founding of World Labs:** **Dr. Fei-Fei Li** explains that she co-founded **World Labs in early 2024** to build foundation models focused on **spatial and physical intelligence**. The company aims to generate 3D and 4D environments to empower creators, aid architectural design, and provide training grounds for robotics.

### ## Public Discourse, Education, and the Next Generation
* **Empowering Educators and Parents:** **Dr. Fei-Fei Li** criticizes Silicon Valley and tech investors for ignoring teachers and parents. Following the launch of ChatGPT in **November 2022**, she immediately emailed her child's elementary school principal to guest lecture and help educators navigate the technology.
* **The Prompting Skill:** **Dr. Fei-Fei Li** compares effective prompt engineering to the **Socratic method**, suggesting that schools should actively teach students how to ask precise questions to extract maximum value from AI tools.

---

### ## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Dr. Fei-Fei Li** predicts that **within 30 years**, robots will become integrated parts of society to assist with physical labor, eldercare, and natural disaster response (such as fighting wildfires).

### ## Notable Quotes
> "The biggest thing humanity never learns is the older generation lamenting about the future generation as if the future generation doesn't know anything... But fundamentally I'm an optimist in humanity."
> — *Dr. Fei-Fei Li*

> "AI learns from patterns. When the patterns are not abundant, then we have to be careful. We have to know how to use AI or how not to use AI."
> — *Dr. Fei-Fei Li*

> "The machine said that because it has learned through pattern when someone tells it 'I'm sick,' you should say 'I'm sorry you're sick' instead of 'I'm so glad you're sick' because that data exists. Whereas your friend who hears that, they genuinely want your well-being."
> — *Dr. Fei-Fei Li*
